title: Read a value, prediction, or residual off the plot
subtitle: Two-variable data: Models and scatterplots · 12 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **12 of the official questions in Two-variable data: Models and scatterplots are this one** — 10 Easy, 2 Medium, 0 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:

- The question names one specific x-value, such as a time, temperature, or distance, and asks what the line of best fit predicts, what a data point's value was, or how far an actual point is from the prediction.
- The answer is a single reading from the graph, often grid-in or rounded to the nearest 5 or 10.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Find the given x-value on the horizontal axis, using the axis label to confirm which variable it is.
- 2) Go straight up to the line if the question says 'predicted', or to the dot if it says 'actual' or 'recorded', then read across to the y-axis.
- 3) For a residual, subtract predicted from actual at the same x.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You read the data point when the question asked for the line's prediction, or the other way round.
You also misread a gridline when each square is worth more than 1 unit, or read the wrong axis in a context where both axes use similar numbers.
